topic: Dietary Synergy: Vitamin C and Iron
questionText:
Read the following case study on adolescent public health nutrition and answer the questions that follow:

During an annual health screening at a government girls' senior secondary school, the medical team tests hemoglobin levels across 300 adolescent girls. The screening reveals that 62% of the girls suffer from Nutritional Anemia (hemoglobin < 12.0 g/dL), with 15% categorized as moderately to severely anemic (< 10.0 g/dL). Teachers report that many anemic students experience chronic lethargy, difficulty concentrating in class, frequent headaches, and poor academic scores. Physical inspection demonstrates conjunctival pallor and pale nail beds. The school implements the national 'Anemia Mukt Bharat' protocol:
1. Administering Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFAS) using blue IFA tablets (100 mg elemental iron + 500 mcg folic acid) on fixed days (Wednesdays).
2. Conducting biannual deworming with Albendazole (400 mg) tablets on National Deworming Day.
3. Counseling students to consume iron-rich dietary sources (green leafy vegetables, jaggery, sprouted pulses) paired with Vitamin C rich amla and guava, while avoiding tea and coffee immediately before or after meals.

Question: Why did the health team instruct students to consume amla, guava, or lemon juice alongside iron-rich meals?

options.text: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) binds with dietary calcium and phytates, preventing their interference with digestive enzymes during nutrient breakdown
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) reduces ferric iron (Fe3+) to soluble ferrous iron (Fe2+), vastly enhancing non-heme iron absorption in the intestine
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately solves the problem for Dietary Synergy: Vitamin C and Iron.

options.text: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) stimulates thyroid hormone secretion, accelerating cell metabolism and hemoglobin synthesis in bone marrow
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) neutralizes gastric hydrochloric acid, preventing premature oxidation of dietary minerals before reaching the liver
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
For Dietary Synergy: Vitamin C and Iron (Nutrition, Food Science and Technology):
Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) acts as a reducing agent, converting insoluble ferric iron (Fe3+) into the soluble ferrous state (Fe2+), which is readily absorbed in the small intestine. Options A, C, and D present scientifically incorrect physiological roles of Vitamin C.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Read the following community nutrition survey case study and answer the questions that follow:

A team of public health nutritionists conducts an epidemiological survey across 500 under-five children in an aspirational tribal district. Using calibrated infantometers, stadiometers, and electronic scales, the team computes anthropometric Z-scores against WHO Child Growth Standards. The survey uncovers startling data:
1. Stunting (Low Height-for-Age < -2 SD): 44% of children suffer from chronic linear growth faltering.
2. Wasting (Low Weight-for-Height < -2 SD): 22% suffer from acute undernutrition, with 6% classified as Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM, < -3 SD).
3. Clinical examination reveals Bitot spots in 4.2% of children, and pallor indicative of Iron Deficiency Anemia in 68% of children.
The nutrition team presents an urgent action blueprint: revitalizing local Anganwadi supplementary feeding, establishing a hospital-based Nutritional Rehabilitation Centre (NRC) for complicated SAM cases, administering megadose Vitamin A prophylaxis, and distributing Double Fortified Salt (DFS) alongside Weekly Iron and Folic Acid Supplementation (WIFAS).

Question: Why did the team recommend Double Fortified Salt (DFS) for community distribution?

options.text: It combines essential calcium and vitamin D to treat childhood rickets and improve bone mineral density across rural communities.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Inverts the governing property or boundary condition.

options.text: It simultaneously delivers bioavailable iron to combat anemia and iodine to prevent goitre and cognitive impairment through a single daily staple.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Correct answer. Accurately identifies the verified NCERT concept for Double Fortified Salt (DFS) Function.

options.text: It integrates high doses of vitamin C and zinc to boost overall immunity against recurrent respiratory and gastrointestinal infections.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: It provides fortified pro-vitamin A carotenoids alongside folic acid to eliminate childhood night blindness and neural tube defects.
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
According to NCERT principles for Nutrition, Food Science and Technology (Double Fortified Salt (DFS) Function):
It simultaneously delivers bioavailable iron to combat anemia and iodine to prevent goitre and cognitive impairment through a single daily staple.

Detailed Context:
Double Fortified Salt (DFS) co-fortifies everyday edible salt with both iodine and bioavailable iron, attacking two pervasive micronutrient deficiencies—goitre/cognitive impairment and anemia—concurrently through a single dietary vehicle. Hence Option A is correct.

Therefore, option (B) is the correct answer.

questionText:
Match the food spoilage agent in List I with its deteriorating effect in List II:

List I:
(A) Food Enzymes (e.g. Polyphenol oxidase)
(B) Psychrotrophic Bacteria (e.g. Pseudomonas)
(C) Oxidative Atmospheric Oxygen
(D) Molds and Yeasts

List II:
(I) Enzymatic browning in cut apples and potatoes
(II) Slime formation, putrefaction, and off-odors in refrigerated raw meat and milk
(III) Oxidative rancidity, lipid peroxidation, and off-flavors in fats and oils
(IV) Fuzzy mycelial growth and alcoholic fermentation in high-sugar jams and breads

topic: Thermal Food Processing Methods and Parameters
questionText:
Match the thermal process in List I with its operational definition in List II:

List I:
(A) Blanching
(B) Pasteurization
(C) Sterilization
(D) Ultra-High Temperature (UHT)

List II:
(I) Mild heat treatment (85-95°C) of vegetables to inactivate enzymes prior to freezing
(II) Heat treatment below 100°C to destroy vegetative pathogens and extend refrigerated shelf life
(III) Severe heat treatment (>100°C) destroying all viable microorganisms and bacterial spores
(IV) Thermal processing at 135-150°C for 1 to 2 seconds for aseptic packaging and room-temperature storage

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III

options.text: A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Applies an adjacent or reciprocal mathematical relation.

options.text: A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV

options.text: A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
options.mistakeAnalysis: Incorrect option. Confuses related NCERT concepts or attributes.

detailedSolution:
Detailed Solution:
Blanching inactivates enzymes, pasteurization kills vegetative pathogens, sterilization destroys all microbes/spores, and UHT enables shelf-stable aseptic milk.
Hence Option A is correct.
Hence, option (C) is the correct match.
